stories.headline: Tokyo Swift did not win Week 1. It annexed it.
stories.body:
F&F: Tokyo Swift opened the season with 199.76 points, an 11-0 all-play record and a 101.50-point demolition of Kool-Aid Man. It was the highest score in the league by 21.94 points, and the lineup was only 94% efficient. That is the cleanest opening statement on the board.

The first tier is already visible behind it. I HURT MY NABERS scored 177.82 with a perfect lineup, while Team Carlzyn put up 167.96 despite operating at 87% efficiency. One week is not a season, but one week was enough to make the rest of the league start negotiating with the evidence.

takes.text: First in scoring, first in all-play, and a win to go with it. That is the whole resume and Cody earned every line of it. But I have been on teams that hung forty in September and spent October explaining it. The Week 2 projection says 130.5. That is the number that tells you who somebody is.

Cody scored 199.76 and somehow the interesting team is still Chase. I HURT MY NABERS started the exact right lineup, scored 177.82 and now gets Carlzyn. Win that one and I will say what everybody else is afraid to say.
Kool-Aid Man lost by 101.50 points. That is not a matchup result. That is a before-and-after photo.

stories.storyline: Can Tokyo Swift turn the league's loudest Week 1 into a weekly advantage, or was 199.76 the opening-week ceiling?

stories.headline: Carlzyn left 82.3 on the bench and still won by 67.4
stories.body:
Team Carlzyn had the league's largest bench total at 82.3 points, including 31.2 from Tyler Shough, and still beat Bakers Dozen 167.96 to 100.56. The lineup captured only 87% of the best score available, but the margin made the mistakes decorative.

The same indulgence was not available everywhere. Kool-Aid Man posted the league's worst lineup efficiency at 75%, leaving 33.1 points outside the best available lineup in a week it scored 98.26. Hunter I hardly know her! left 20.5 points outside the best lineup and lost by 8.12. One manager had enough roster to survive the wrong answers. The others simply had wrong answers.

takes.text: Bench points and lineup inefficiency are not interchangeable, which is why I care about the 25.6 points Carlzyn left outside its best lineup more than the raw 82.3 sitting on the bench. The alarming part for everyone else is that 167.96 was the inefficient version.
Mason scored 167.96 while misplacing a quarter-century of usable points. Bakers Dozen scored 100.56 at 97% efficiency. One manager needs lineup advice. The other needs players.
Perfect efficiency is a trap. Chase used every point correctly in Week 1, which means there is nowhere left to improve. Carlzyn has 25.6 points of untapped upside. I would rather have the mistakes.

stories.storyline: Is Carlzyn's inefficient 167.96 a warning that the roster has another gear, or the kind of weekly lineup puzzle that eventually costs a win?

stories.headline: $20 bought Vele. $30 bought Tyler a personality.
stories.body:
David landed Devaughn Vele for $20, beating bids of $15 from I HURT MY NABERS and Return of the King and $10 from Dsteady1234. It was the only contested paid claim of the week, and it left davidbatista with $80 of FAAB.

Return of the King spent $15 each on Antonio Williams and Dontayvion Wicks, leaving $70. Tyler also submitted two $0 claims for Bryce Young, losing one and winning the other, which is either procedural sophistication or evidence that the waiver screen won. Meanwhile, Tokyo Swift responded to 199.76 points by making five Week 2 add-drop moves. Apparently comfort is for teams below 190.

takes.text: Tyler spent more than David and still let David take the only player four teams fought over. If Wicks and Antonio Williams are the master plan, I want it laminated so we can preserve the evidence.

David paid $20 for the one man four teams wanted and still walked away with $80 in his pocket. Tyler spent thirty percent of his budget on two guys nobody was bidding against. I have watched front offices do both. Only one of them is still answering the phone in December.
The double Bryce Young claim was intentional. Tyler forced the system to reveal which Bryce Young wanted it more. He now has the motivated one.

stories.storyline: Will David's contested $20 bet on Devaughn Vele outperform Tyler's two $15 waiver additions?

stories.headline: Week 2 puts the first tier in the same room
stories.body:
I HURT MY NABERS and Team Carlzyn meet after finishing second and third in Week 1 scoring. Carlzyn carries the slightly higher current projection, 136.1 to 131.3, while NABERS brings the league's only 100% efficient opening lineup. Somebody in the early top three is taking a loss.

Elsewhere, the projections are trying to move faster than the standings. Littlescot229 owns the highest current Week 2 projection at 138.8 after scoring 129.64 in Week 1. Bakers Dozen projects for 135.2 after a 100.56-point opener. Tokyo Swift, after nearly touching 200, is projected for 128.8 against Return of the King at 122.2. Every player in all six matchups is still to play, so these are forecasts, not alibis.

takes.text: The Carlzyn-NABERS spread is 4.8 points, which is functionally a coin flip in a league where the public quarterback projections are still built around four-point passing touchdowns. I do not trust the precision, but I trust the matchup.
Carlzyn had 82.3 on the bench and everybody decided that means depth. It can also mean Mason has too many ways to get cute. Chase already proved he can submit the right ten.
Bakers Dozen is scoring 135.2 this week because the projection says 135.2 and projections only become unreliable after kickoff. David should prepare accordingly.

stories.storyline: Does the Week 2 Carlzyn-NABERS matchup produce a genuine challenger to Tokyo Swift at the top?

stories.headline: The six-point quarterback argument has its first receipts
stories.body:
The league pays six points for a passing touchdown, while the public projection set behind the briefing assumes four. That gap remains the desk's standing dispute with every clean-looking weekly total.

The first week did not settle the argument, but Week 2 gives it useful pressure points. Josh Allen is projected for 25.2 in Carlzyn's matchup with I HURT MY NABERS, Dak Prescott for 24.6 against Hunter I hardly know her!, and Brock Purdy for 24.0 against Tokyo Swift. If quarterback scoring is being systematically understated, the closest projected matchups are where the missing points should become hardest to ignore.

takes.text: Every quarterback number anybody quotes in this league is built on a four-point touchdown, and this league pays six. I am not a numbers man. I do not have to be. When the ruler is wrong you stop arguing about the inches.
I said three to four points per quarterback per week, and nothing in the briefing has disproved it. The numbers are not neutral just because they arrive with a decimal.
The quarterback projections are wrong, everybody knows why they are wrong, and six managers will still cite them after losing. We have invented a spreadsheet-shaped horoscope.

stories.storyline: Does the six-point passing touchdown actually reshape quarterback value in this league, or does everyone keep drafting and starting as if it pays four?
